subject: social-studies
general_outcomes: By the end of Junior School, the learner should be able to:
demonstrate an understanding of historical concepts, historical sources, and evidence for the development of identity and a sense of belonging.
develop Life Skills to navigate through challenges in day-to-day life.
conserve and manage the environment for sustainable development.
manage pertinent and contemporary issues as an informed, engaged, empowered, ethical, and responsive citizen.
apply research and digital literacy competencies to interpret phenomena for problem-solving and decision-making in society.
apply values, positive attitudes, principles of democracy, governance, and human rights for mutual social responsibility.
appreciate themselves, and other people, be proud of their kenyan cultural heritage, and be willing to further develop, preserve, and share this heritage globally.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to explore personal abilities and interests for self-improvement.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: Learner explores personal abilities and interests for self-improvement with examples.
assessment_rubric.meets: Learner explores personal abilities and interests for self-improvement.
assessment_rubric.approaches: Learner explores personal abilities and interests for self-improvement omitting a few details.
assessment_rubric.below: Learner explores personal abilities and interests for self-improvement omitting many details.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: Learner identifies entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality using examples.
assessment_rubric.meets: Learner identifies entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality.
assessment_rubric.approaches: Learner identifies entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality leaving out a few of them.
assessment_rubric.below: Learner identifies entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality leaving out many of them.

substrands.name: Self-Exploration
learning_outcomes: explore personal abilities and interests for holistic development
develop personal values for a steady personality
manage emotions in day-to-day life
appreciate personal awareness in day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: reflect and journal personal abilities and interests and share with a friend in class
brainstorm on how to use personal abilities and interests for holistic development and make presentations in class
share personal values that help him or her pull through as a steady person
use print or digital resources to search for how to develop personal principles and share in class
search using digital or print media how to manage emotions (happiness, love, fear, and anger) in day-to-day life
share previous experiences in groups how he/she dealt with emotions
watch relevant video clips or print media on effective management of emotions in day-to-day life.
inquiry_questions: How can personal abilities and interests influence career choices?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: learners reflect and journal personal abilities and interests and share them with a friend in class.
Critical Thinking and Problem-solving: learners share previous experiences in groups and how he or she dealt with emotions. Values:
Unity: learners brainstorm on how to use personal abilities and interests for holistic development and make presentations in class.

Responsibility: learners use print or digital resources to search for how to develop personal principles and share in class. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Decision-making skills: Learners reflect and journal personal abilities and interests hence and with a friend in class. Link to other Subjects: English/Kiswahili/KSL: learners use speaking and listening skills to brainstorm on personal abilities and interests for holistic development.

substrands.name: Entrepreneurial Opportunities in Social Studies
learning_outcomes: identify entrepreneurial opportunities that closely match their personality
describe requirements for social entrepreneurial opportunities in the world of work
appreciate entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies.
learning_experiences: using digital or print media to search and classify entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies and make a presentation in class
create posters of common entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies and display them in class
use digital or print media to find out the personality requirements for any five social studies entrepreneurial opportunities in day-to-day life and make presentations in class
draw charts showing an alignment of personal talents or abilities with different entrepreneurial opportunities in the country
• engage a relevant resource person to give a talk on entrepreneurial opportunities versus personality types
inquiry_questions: 1. What is entrepreneurship 2. Which entrepreneurial opportunities exist in society?
core_competencies: Creativity and Imagination: learners create posters of common entrepreneurial opportunities in social studies and display them in class.
Digital Literacy: learners use digital or print resources to explore entrepreneurial opportunities in Social Studies.
values: Responsibility: learners create a poster of all entrepreneurial opportunities available in Social Studies and display it in school.
pertinent_issues: Career exploration: learners draw charts aligning personal talents and abilities with available entrepreneurial opportunities.
Decision-making Skills: learners develop analytical and critical thinking skills as they use digital or print resources to explore entrepreneurial opportunities in Social Studies.
links_to_other_areas: Pre-Technical Studies: learners draw charts aligning personal talents and abilities with available entrepreneurial opportunities.

substrands.name: Developments in Medium of trade
learning_outcomes: compare barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa
trace the factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa
deduce the impact of the introduction of money in Africa
appreciate the medium of trade for sustainability.
learning_experiences: discuss the comparison between barter trade and the use of currency in Africa
use digital /print media to find out factors that led to the introduction of money in Africa
brainstorm on the impact of the introduction of money in Africa
engage a resource person to give a talk on the impact of the introduction of money in Africa
role play barter trade and the use of currency trade in Africa and provide a critique.
inquiry_questions: How has money transformed trade in Africa?
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: learners speak effectively and logically as they compare barter trade and use of currency in Africa.
values: Respect: learners develop acceptance as they listen to each other as they brainstorm on the impact of the introduction of money in Africa.
pertinent_issues: Self-awareness: learners role play a barter trade and the use of currency.
links_to_other_areas: Pre-Technical Studies: Learners apply knowledge gained from the impact of introduction of currency in Africa.

substrands.name: Human Origin
learning_outcomes: explore traditional stories of human origin from African communities
explain religious stories about the origin of humankind
illustrate common aspects found in traditional and religious stories of human origin
acknowledge religious and traditional stories of human origin.
learning_experiences: engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human origin from different communities
compare the different stories on human origin from their communities and share in class
write a collaborative essay on traditional and religious stories of human origin
record traditional stories about the origin of humankind in society
use relevant print or electronic media, resources to research and present in class the traditional and religious stories about the origin of humankind
discuss ways of recording traditional stories about the origin of humankind in society.
• discuss the implications of the traditional and religious stories on human origin.
inquiry_questions: How did human beings come to be?
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: learners engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human origin from different communities.
values: Respect: learners discuss in turn the implications of the traditional and religious stories on human origin.
pertinent_issues: Social Awareness: learners relate with others well as they compare different stories on human origin.
links_to_other_areas: Religious Education: learners relate with creation stories as they engage a resource person to discuss the traditional and religious stories on human origin.

substrands.name: Early Civilisation
learning_outcomes: explore factors that led to the growth of the selected ancient Kingdoms in Africa
locate the selected ancient Kingdoms on a map of Africa
assess the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the modern world civilisation
appreciate the contribution of ancient kingdoms to the development of the modern world.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on factors that led to the growth of ancient Egypt, Great Zimbabwe, and the Kingdom of Kongo
use appropriate digital or print media to find out the location of ancient Egypt, Great Zimbabwe, and the Kingdom of Kongo from the map of Africa
watch and critique audio-visual documentary on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation
write an essay on the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the development of the modern world civilisation and present it in class.
inquiry_questions: How has early African civilisation influenced the world today?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be Developed: Critical thinking: learners watch and critique audio-visual documentaries on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation. Values: Unity: learners watch and critique audio-visual documentaries on the contribution of Ancient Kingdoms to modern world civilisation. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Self-esteem: learners write and present in class an essay on the contribution of ancient Kingdoms to the development of modern world civilisation. Link to other Learning Areas: Creative Arts: learners relate the ancient contribution of Ancient to the modern world civilisation, by applying knowledge drawn from architectural designs, dressing, and artefacts.

substrands.name: Slavery and Servitude
learning_outcomes: identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society
explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade
sketch the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa
desire to promote human dignity for a just and peaceful world.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of slavery and servitude and share their findings in class
discuss various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society
use digital or print resources to find out the factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade
draw the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean Slave trade in Africa
develop slogans on ways of promoting human dignity for a just and peaceful world and share in class.
inquiry_questions: Why has slavery and servitude existed for thousands of years?
core_competencies: Core Competencies:
Communication and Collaboration: learners contribute to group decision-making as they brainstorm on the meaning of slavery and servitude and share their findings in class.

Learning to Learn: learners use digital learning platforms for continuous learning and development as they use appropriate digital devices to draw and show the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa. Values:
Unity: learners work in groups to brainstorm on various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society.

Responsibility: learners observe safety precautions as they use print or digital resources to locate the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs):

Human Rights: learners identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society and locate areas where slaves were taken during the Indian Ocean slave trade, Link to other Learning Areas: Learners use speaking skills as they brainstorm on forms of slavery and servitude.

substrands.name: Diversity and interpersonal relationships
learning_outcomes: identify factors that determine human diversity in the society
explain interpersonal skills that enhance healthy interactions in a multicultural society
classify the desirable and undesirable personality attributes
appreciate the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on what is human diversity
use digital or print materials to search for factors that determine human diversity
debate and classify desirable and undesirable personality attributes
role play in class the personality attributes that enhance self-awareness
outline personality attributes to enhance self-awareness
engage a resource person to discuss life skills that would promote healthy interactions in a multicultural society (effective communication, negotiation skills, Assertiveness, empathy)
research using appropriate print, library resources, or digital devices on the components of
human identity in a multicultural society
role-play the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society.
inquiry_questions: 1. How do varied personalities shape society?
2. Why is respect and appreciation of diversity crucial for social cohesion?
core_competencies: Self-efficacy: learners debate and classify desirable and undesirable personality attributes.
Learning to Learn: learners develop relationship skills as they role-play the importance of building healthy relationships in a multicultural society.
values: Respect: learners develop acceptance as they listen to each other and brainstorm personality attributes that make individuals different from others.
pertinent_issues: Self-esteem: learners develop creative skills as they compose and recite poems that propagate inclusion and diversity.
Self-awareness: learners role play the personality attributes to enhance self-awareness.
links_to_other_areas: English/Kiswahili/KSL: learners brainstorm on desirable and undesirable personality attributes.

substrands.name: Peaceful Coexistence
learning_outcomes: outline the qualities of a peaceful person in the community
explore factors that promote peaceful co-existence
assess peaceful conflict resolution process in day-to-day life
value the importance of peaceful coexistence in the community in day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: Learner is guided to:
brainstorm on the qualities of a peaceful person in the community
write an essay on the qualities of a peaceful person
use digital or print resources to find out peaceful conflict resolution process
engage a resource person to give a talk on factors that promote peaceful co-existence
role play in peaceful conflict resolution process in day-to-day life
compose and recite peace poems on the importance of peaceful co-existence in the community in day-to-day life.
inquiry_questions: 1. How can we promote peace for mutual social well-being?
2. How can I manage stress and emotion to promote inner peace?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:

Digital Literacy: learners use digital or print resources to find out the peaceful conflict resolution processes. Values: Peace: learners role play peaceful conflict resolution process in day-to-day life. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs): Social Cohesion: learners write down what they plan to do to improve inner peace and relationships with their family, school, or community. Link to other Learning Areas: Learners use creative skills to compose and recite peace poems in class.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to explain the steps in a CSL project/activity.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: Learner explains the steps in a CSL project exhaustively.
assessment_rubric.meets: Learner explains the steps in a CSL project.
assessment_rubric.approaches: Learner explains most of the details in the CSL project.
assessment_rubric.below: Learner explains a few of the steps in the CSL project.

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to accomplish a CSL project/activity in group(s).
assessment_rubric.exceeds: Learner accomplished a CSL project/activity in group(s) excellently.
assessment_rubric.meets: Learner accomplished a CSL project/activity in group(s).
assessment_rubric.approaches: Learner did not complete the CSL project/activity in group(s).
assessment_rubric.below: Learner did not attempt the CSL project/activity in group(s).

assessment_rubric.indicator: Ability to explain the importance of CSL in the community.
assessment_rubric.exceeds: Learner explains clearly the importance of CSL in the community.
assessment_rubric.meets: Learner explains the importance of CSL in the community.
assessment_rubric.approaches: Learner explains fairly the importance of CSL in the community.
assessment_rubric.below: Learner hardly explains the importance of CSL in the community.

substrands.name: Community Service Learning
learning_outcomes: explain the meaning of key terms used in community service learning (CSL) and CSL projects
describe the importance of CSL in the community
outline steps of a CSL project/activity
execute a class CSL project
desire to conduct CSL projects in the community.
learning_experiences: Learner is guided to:

brainstorm on the meaning of the terms community, community services, community service learning (CSL), project (activities outside class), problem (gaps or opportunities), solution (remedy), plan of activity, implementation, and written report of a project.

discuss the steps involved in carrying out a CSL project: -identification and verification of a problem/gap/opportunity -planning to solve an identified problem -designing solution(s) to the problem -implementing the solution/filling the gap -reflecting and reporting on the project/activity done
identify and brainstorm on problems/gaps in their context/community.
discuss, verify, and adopt one problem for the class/group project.
propose and plan way(s) of solving the problem.
implement the solution to the problem in the community.
write and report on the accomplished project
discuss CSL benefits for self and the community.
inquiry_questions: How can community service learning contribute to community development?
core_competencies: Communication and Collaboration: learners develop skills of listening keenly and effectively as they discuss and brainstorm on types of projects and identification of relevant community problems.
Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learners develop the skill of exploring complex problems as they identify projects that can be undertaken in the community.
Self-efficacy: learners develop self-awareness skills as they consider the steps in a CSL project and propose ways in which they can present CSL findings.
values: Love: learners develop selflessness as they engage in a discussion on the benefits of CSL for self and community.
Responsibility: learners develop self-drive as they implement the solution to the problem in the community
links_to_other_areas: All subjects as they provide PCIs and undertake CSL activities.

substrands.name: Historical information
learning_outcomes: identify various sources of historical information in the society
distinguish between primary and secondary sources of historical information
explore how various sources of historical information have been preserved over the years
appreciate the significance of various sources of historical information in providing evidence of past human accounts.
learning_experiences: Learner is guided to:
use appropriate print media or digital resources to identify sources of historical information in society and share in class
design posters on primary and secondary sources of historical information in society and display them in class
watch documentaries or video clips on the ways of preserving sources of historical information.
debate on the significance of various sources of historical information in providing evidence of past human accounts.
inquiry_questions: How significant are sources of historical information in understanding past human accounts?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: learners express themselves with clarity as they debate on the significance of historical information.
Digital Literacy: learners use digital technology to effectively accomplish their tasks as they find out the sources of historical information using appropriate media. Values:
Patriotism: learners develop dedication as they debate on the significance of various sources of historical information in providing evidence of past human accounts.
Responsibility: learners diligently use appropriate print media or digital resources to find out sources of historical information. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs):
Social Cohesion: learners debate as a class on the significance of historical sources of information in society. Link to other Subjects:
Learners apply listening and speaking skills as they discuss in small groups, sources of historical information in the society.
Learners apply creative skills as they design posters on primary and secondary sources of historical information in society.

substrands.name: Historical Development of Agriculture
learning_outcomes: locate areas where early agriculture was practised in selected geographical regions in Africa
explore factors that favoured growing of crops and rearing of animals in selected regions during early agriculture
assess the contributions of the Nile Valley agriculture to the world civilisation
value the importance of domestication of plants and animals in Africa.

use digital devices/ other sources to draw the map of Africa and show areas where early agriculture was practised in selected geographical regions. (Rift Valley of Eastern Africa, Egypt, and Nubia)
discuss the contribution of the Nile Valley agriculture to the world civilisation
compose poems the importance of domestication of plants and animals in Africa.
Suggested Learning Experiences
inquiry_questions: 1. Why did people start practising agriculture in Africa?
2. How did Agriculture begin in Africa?

Question(s)
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:

Digital Literacy: learners carry out research on the factors that favoured growing of crops and rearing of animals in selected regions during early agriculture,(in Egypt, Nubia, and in the Rift Valley of the Eastern African region and report the findings to the class

Communication and collaboration: Learners apply listening and speaking skills as they compose poems the importance of domestication of plants and animals in Africa. Social Cohesion: learners discuss the contribution of the Nile Valley agriculture to the world civilisation, Link to other Subjects:

Learners use knowledge of animal husbandry as they research on animals kept and types of crops which were grown during early agriculture in Egypt, Nubia and in Rift valley of the Eastern African region.

substrands.name: Maps and map work
learning_outcomes: describe the position, shape, and size of Africa
locate places and features using latitudes and longitudes on a map
calculate the time of different places in the world
appreciate the location of key features in the continent.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on the position, shape, and size of Africa and share in class
buzz on the countries that make up Africa and display in class
draw an outline map of Africa creatively and indicate the countries that make up Africa and display it in class
use relevant print media or digital devices to establish the position and location of places and features on a map
calculate the time of different places using longitudes
discuss and appreciate positive features that are associated with Africa.
inquiry_questions: 1. How are maps used?
2. Why is time different in various locations?
core_competencies: Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital Literacy: learners apply the skill of designing and creating new digital artefacts, content, and materials as they establish the position and location of places and features on a map.
Creativity and Imagination: learners undertake group activities and exchange new ideas that inspire creative thinking as they draw an outline map of Africa. Values:
Responsibility: learners develop diligence as they research the three types of maps used in Social Studies and make summary notes.
Patriotism: learners develop loyalty as they draw an outline map of Africa and indicate the countries that makeup Africa.
Unity: learners demonstrate fairness as they brainstorm the position, shape, and size of Africa. Pertinent and Contemporary Issues (PCIs):
Social Cohesion: learners brainstorm on the position, shape, and size of Africa.

Environmental Education: learners use latitudes to locate the position of places and features on a map. Link to other Subjects: Learners apply calculation skills as they use longitudes to calculate the time of different places in the world.

substrands.name: Earth and the Solar System

explore the size, shape, and position of the Earth in the solar system
examine the effects of rotation and revolution of the earth on human activities
illustrate the internal structure of the earth in the solar system
appreciate the effects of rotation and revolution of the earth on human activities.

use relevant print or digital resources to find out about the theories explaining the origin of the earth (the passing star theory and the nebula cloud theory)
brainstorm on the size, shape, and position of the earth in the solar system
carry out library research on the effects of rotation and revolution of the earth on human activities

values: Respect: learners demonstrate humility as they share stories on the origin of the earth.
pertinent_issues: Environmental Education: learners examine the effects of rotation and revolution of the earth on human activities.
Social Cohesion: learners share stories on the origin of the earth from their communities.
links_to_other_areas: Learners apply computing skills as they use relevant print or digital resources to find out the theories explaining the origin of the earth.

substrands.name: Weather

construct selected instruments for measuring elements of weather
examine the significance of weather to the human environment
respond appropriately to different weather conditions in the environment.
learning_experiences: use relevant print or digital resources to research the elements of weather in the environment and write a report
record and calculate weather conditions in the local environment (temperature, rainfall)
discuss the factors considered when constructing and siting a weather station in the school compound
use locally available materials to construct selected instruments for measuring elements of weather (a rain gauge/ wind vane/windsock) and peer assess

discuss the effects of weather on road safety
invite a resource person from a meteorological station to discuss possible careers related to climate.

Question(s)

pertinent_issues: Safety and Security: learners acquire knowledge of weather elements and respond appropriately to different weather conditions.
Decision-making: learners discuss the factors to consider when constructing and setting a weather station in the school compound.
links_to_other_areas: Learners record and calculate weather conditions in the local environment.

substrands.name: Fieldwork
